experiments.carry_reason: The event's costings end before the population's first year. The measure is a permanent change of level whose last costing year is steady state, so later years compare with that year, scaled to the run year's base.
experiments.magnitude_reason: The limit applies to children born from 6 April 2017, so its yield grows each year until every child is covered; the 2020-21 costing is not steady state.
experiments.note: Removes the two-child limit in 2024-25 and 2025-26 (a child count of 100 stands for none). Modern law abolishes it from April 2026 (Autumn Budget 2025), so later years have nothing to move.
sources: Welfare Reform and Work Act 2016 s. 13-14

experiments.note: Restores the CPI upratings the four-year freeze forwent (April 2017-2019: 1.0%, 3.0%, 2.4%; April 2016's was nil): the Universal Credit standard allowances and child elements, child benefit, working-age housing benefit allowances and tax credit elements, each at its modern value times 1.065267. Disability and carer elements were outside the freeze. Missing legs: local housing allowance rates and legacy JSA, ESA and income support.
sources: Welfare Reform and Work Act 2016 s. 11 and Sch. 1
